# lean-pkg receipt comparator

run the comparator on a Lake project and write the comparator receipt (the `comparator-receipt` program: the same code and flags).

Also run as the program `comparator-receipt`: the same code and flags.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg receipt comparator [--repo DIR] [--check CHECK]
                            [--mechanism {auto,toolchain,legacy}] [--verify VERIFY]
                            [--evidence-dir DIR] [--prepare] [--from-prepared DIR]
                            [--no-resume] [--judges N] [--unit-size K] [--slots SPEC]
                            [--estimate] [--sample K] [--force-sample]
                            [--verify-oleans [DIR]] [--attempts [DIR]]
                            [--seal-sacct RECEIPT] [--sacct-file F] [--user NAME]
                            [--json] [--host-label LABEL] [--json]
```

Run comparator-check.sh and write a comparator receipt. The same code and flags as the `comparator-receipt` program, which stays.

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--repo DIR` | the package checkout, a Lake project directory (default: cwd) (old spelling --project, kept working). Default: `.`. |
| `--check CHECK` | comparator-check.sh to run (env COMPARATOR_CHECK; default: the copy shipped with lean-pkg) |
| `--mechanism {auto,toolchain,legacy}` | toolchain: `lake comparator` with the toolchain's bundled kernels (Lean v4.35.0-rc2+, what Palomar runs); legacy: the pinned comparator/lean4export/nanoda/landrun stack; auto (default): toolchain when available, else legacy. Choices: `auto`, `toolchain`, `legacy`. |
| `--verify VERIFY` | verify-comparator.sh for the toolchain mechanism (env COMPARATOR_VERIFY; default: the vendored PalomarTemplate copy) |
| `--evidence-dir DIR` | where the stage logs and stages.json go, kept on failure (default: &lt;project&gt;/.lake/comparator-receipt; its comparator-stages/ subdirectory); outside the project its path is written as &lt;evidence&gt; in every log and receipt |
| `--prepare` | run only the setup stages (dependency checkout, Mathlib cache, build of the configured modules); idempotent; a later run at the same commit, toolchain and config hash skips them and runs only the comparison |
| `--from-prepared DIR` | reuse the completed setup recorded in DIR (an evidence directory or its stages.json); refuses when it was prepared for another commit/toolchain/config |
| `--no-resume` | judge every slot again, ignoring the slots this commit and config hash already accepted (cached under &lt;evidence-dir&gt;/comparator-stages/04-slots/) |
| `--judges N` | run up to N judge processes at once, each on a contiguous shard of every configuration's theorem_names (toolchain mechanism; env LEAN_PKG_COMPARATOR_JOBS; default 1); with --unit-size, N is only how many units run at once. The merged verdict is exact; see docs/comparator.md (Runtime) for when it helps |
| `--unit-size K` | judge each configuration in contiguous units of at most K names (toolchain mechanism; env LEAN_PKG_COMPARATOR_UNIT_SIZE; default: the whole configuration, cut into --judges shards). --unit-size 1 --judges 1 judges each name alone, one at a time, so a capped run resumes per name |
| `--slots SPEC` | judge only these slots (theorem_names entries): comma-separated names, &lt;config&gt;:&lt;name&gt;, 1-based indices or ranges i-j over all configurations, or sample:K (a namespace-stratified sample). Writes a PARTIAL receipt into the stage directory, marked partial: true: diagnostic only, refused as evidence |
| `--estimate` | after setup, judge a sample of slots (the heaviest by olean size, then namespace-stratified) one at a time and print an estimate {per_slot_seconds, slots, estimated_seconds, recommended_cap, remaining_estimate_seconds}; writes no receipt (the judged slots are cached for the real run). The JSON is schema comparator-estimate/2; /1 -&gt; /2 added the sample floor, the heaviest-first sample (per-row weight_bytes, weight_module, heavy) and the max cap model; later additions (weights_found, remaining_estimate_seconds, ...) are additive and keep /2. See docs/comparator.md (Estimate first) |
| `--sample K` | --estimate: sample size (default and floor: max(5, ceil(0.25 \* slots)), capped at the slots); --slots overrides the sample |
| `--force-sample` | --estimate: accept a --sample (or --slots) below the floor; the estimate warns and records sample_forced: true |
| `--verify-oleans [DIR]` | read-only, no host policy: rehash the package's compiled modules under .lake/build/lib and compare them with the olean manifest the setup recorded in DIR (an evidence directory, its comparator-stages/ or its stages.json; default: the evidence directory); the recorded commit must be HEAD; exit 0 same, 1 different or nothing recorded; writes nothing |
| `--attempts [DIR]` | read-only, no host policy: list the earlier runs kept under comparator-stages/attempts/NNN/ (verdict, failed stage, commit, times, files, whether every kept file still matches its recorded sha256) in DIR (an evidence directory, its comparator-stages/ or its attempts/; default: the evidence directory); exit 0, or 1 when a kept file changed or went missing; writes nothing |
| `--seal-sacct RECEIPT` | after the Slurm job finished, no host policy: corroborate RECEIPT's Slurm claim (job_id from SLURM_JOB_ID, which any shell can set) with the job's sacct record: COMPLETED, exit 0:0, Start..End containing the run, this account (live sacct, or --user) and the receipt's node (its h- host label against the node's); writes &lt;c12&gt;-comparator-sacct.txt beside RECEIPT (the record, normalized; no user or node names) and its sha256 into RECEIPT as slurm_sacct. Only a sealed receipt backs a coverage.yaml compute job. Exit 0 sealed (or already), 1 refused, nothing written |
| `--sacct-file F` | --seal-sacct on a host without Slurm: the saved output of `SLURM_TIME_FORMAT=%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z sacct -j J --format=JobID,State,ExitCode,Start,End,Elapsed,User,NodeList -P` (with its header line); the account is then checked only with --user |
| `--user NAME` | --seal-sacct: the account the job must have run under (default with live sacct: this one); compared, never written |
| `--json` | --estimate, --verify-oleans, --attempts or --seal-sacct: print JSON; stdout is the JSON document alone, the progress goes to stderr |
| `--host-label LABEL` | name the host LABEL in the receipt (host, host_label, job_id, host_policy) and the output (env COMPARATOR_RECEIPT_HOST_LABEL); default: h- and 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the lower-cased host name, the label `receipt systemd` uses; the host name itself is never written |

## Details

`lean-pkg receipt comparator [--repo DIR] [--check SCRIPT] [--mechanism M] [--evidence-dir DIR] [--prepare | --from-prepared DIR]` is the separate console
script that produces comparator receipts; see
[The comparator tier](../comparator.md). `COMPARATOR_RECEIPT_STACK=unlimited|<kB>`
raises the soft stack limit of its `lake`/`lean` children (never above the hard
limit; recorded as the receipt's `stack_limit`); it warns when the soft limit is
8 MiB or less; see [Stack limit](../comparator.md#stages-and---prepare).
`COMPARATOR_RECEIPT_BUILD_SOURCE=TEXT` declares where the package's oleans were
built (a job id or host label; redacted); the receipt's `build_provenance` records
whether the `build` stage compiled anything or found the oleans prebuilt; see
[Build provenance](../comparator.md#stages-and---prepare).
The setup also records an olean manifest (the package's own compiled modules,
hashed into `comparator-stages/03-build.oleans.sha256`; receipt
`olean_manifest`); a reused setup whose oleans changed is refused, and the
comparator stage fails when they change during the comparison.
`lean-pkg receipt comparator --verify-oleans [DIR] [--json]` is the read-only check
(exit 0 same, 1 different or not recorded); see
[Olean manifest](../comparator.md#stages-and---prepare).
A run that replaces an earlier run's stage files first keeps them, read-only,
as `comparator-stages/attempts/NNN/` with an `attempt.json` (numbers never
reused; lean-pkg never deletes or reads them back);
`lean-pkg receipt comparator --attempts [DIR] [--json]` lists them; see
[Attempts](../comparator.md#stages-and---prepare).
A refusal because Lake reported a statement or constant mismatch
(`Challenge and solution theorem statement do not match`,
`Const does not match between challenge and target`) ends with one line
`next: lean-pkg comparator check NAME --contracts-only` (`--repo DIR` when the
run's checkout is not the registered one), printed once per run, and
`stages.json` (and a kept attempt's `--attempts --json` row) records it as
`next_command` (null otherwise); display only, the verdict is unchanged; see
[Mechanisms](../comparator.md#mechanisms) and
[a contracts-only diagnostic](../comparator.md#a-contracts-only-diagnostic).
`lean-pkg receipt comparator --seal-sacct RECEIPT [--sacct-file F] [--user NAME] [--json]`
(no host policy, after the Slurm job finished) corroborates the receipt's Slurm
claim with the job's sacct record and seals it (`slurm_sacct`, and
`<commit12>-comparator-sacct.txt` beside the receipt); only a sealed claim backs a
`coverage.yaml` `compute` job; see
[Seal the Slurm claim with sacct](../comparator.md#seal-the-slurm-claim-with-sacct).
`COMPARATOR_RECEIPT_LEAN_THREADS=N` sets `LEAN_NUM_THREADS=N` for those children
(N = 1 serializes the build on a memory-tight host; recorded as the receipt's
`lean_threads`; any other value exits 2); see
[Serial builds](../comparator.md#stages-and---prepare).
`--judges N` (env `LEAN_PKG_COMPARATOR_JOBS`) runs up to N judges at once;
`--unit-size K` (env `LEAN_PKG_COMPARATOR_UNIT_SIZE`) cuts each configuration
into units of at most K names, making `--judges` only the pool width
(`--unit-size 1 --judges 1` judges each name alone, so a capped run resumes
per name; recorded as the receipt's `unit_size`; a value that is not a
positive integer exits 2); see [Unit size](../comparator.md#stages-and---prepare).
`--estimate [--sample K [--force-sample]] [--json]` times a sample of slots and
writes no receipt: the sample is at least `max(5, ceil(0.25 * slots))` (capped at
the slot count) and starts with the heaviest slots by olean size; a smaller
`--sample` (or `--slots` subset) exits 2 unless `--force-sample`, which warns and
records `sample_forced: true`; `recommended_cap` uses the per-slot max model below
half coverage (`cap_model`); `weights_found: false` (with a warning) says no slot
had an olean weight; `remaining_estimate_seconds` covers the unsampled slots only;
the JSON is schema `comparator-estimate/2`; see
[Estimate first](../comparator.md#stages-and---prepare).
`COMPARATOR_RECEIPT_NO_MATHLIB=1` declares a project that knowingly has no Mathlib
dependency; without it the toolchain mechanism refuses such a project before any
stage, and with it `verify-comparator.sh` skips `lake exe cache get`; see
[Mechanisms](../comparator.md#mechanisms).

## Examples

In the package checkout, time a sample of the comparator slots first; no receipt is written.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt comparator --estimate
```

In the package checkout, run the comparator over every configuration and write .lean-receipts/&lt;commit12&gt;-comparator.json (the `comparator-receipt` program does the same).

```bash
lean-pkg receipt comparator
```

The same for another directory, with up to four judges at once.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt comparator --repo src/my-proof --judges 4
```

After the Slurm job finished, seal its sacct record into the receipt so its job can back a compute site.

```bash
lean-pkg receipt comparator --seal-sacct .lean-receipts/cb3d68a21454-comparator.json
```
